text: In Lesson 6, every key and setting in the system came from Vault.

text: In Lesson 9, card numbers were sealed with keys that never leave Vault.

text: This lesson is about who can open Vault itself.
prefix: This lesson is about who can open Vault itself.

text: There is an easier way, and Timur knows it.
prefix: There is an easier way, and Timur knows it.

text: Run an install script once, and keep the master password in a text file on his laptop.
prefix: Run an install script once, and keep the master password in a text file on his laptop.

text: Months later, Timur leaves the bank.
prefix: Months later, Timur leaves the bank.

text: Then a disk fails.
prefix: Then a disk fails.

text: The database backup is there, but nobody can read it, because nobody kept the keys that sealed it.
prefix: The database backup is there, but nobody can read it, because nobody kept the keys that sealed it.

text: One person and one file: the keys end up either lost or leaked.
prefix: One person and one file: the keys end up either lost or leaked.

text: Most teams guard their keys against strangers, and forget the person who installed them.
prefix: Most teams guard their keys against strangers, and forget the person who installed them.

text: I think that person is the bigger risk.
prefix: I think that person is the bigger risk.

text: So Vault opens a different way.
prefix: So Vault opens a different way.

text: At install, Vault's opening key is split into five key shares.
prefix: At install, Vault's opening key is split into five key shares.

text: A key share is one piece of that key, useless on its own.
prefix: A key share is one piece of that key, useless on its own.

text: Any three shares together open Vault.
prefix: Any three shares together open Vault.

text: No one alone can, and no two can either.
prefix: No one alone can, and no two can either.

text: Each share goes to one person: a keyholder.
prefix: Each share goes to one person: a keyholder.

text: A keyholder keeps their share in their own password manager, and nowhere else.
prefix: A keyholder keeps their share in their own password manager, and nowhere else.

text: The bank chooses the keyholders, and makes sure no one holds two shares.
prefix: The bank chooses the keyholders, and makes sure no one holds two shares.

text: Nothing of this ceremony is written down anywhere: not the shares, not on the server, not in a log.
prefix: Nothing of this ceremony is written down anywhere: not the shares, not on the server, not in a log.

text: Vault also locks itself.
prefix: Vault also locks itself.

text: Every time it starts, it starts sealed: it holds everything, but can read nothing.
prefix: Every time it starts, it starts sealed: it holds everything, but can read nothing.

text: To unseal it, three keyholders come, and each types their own share.
prefix: To unseal it, three keyholders come, and each types their own share.

text: Until then, nothing that needs Vault can run.
prefix: Until then, nothing that needs Vault can run.

text: Setting things up needs one more key: a master key for the session.
prefix: Setting things up needs one more key: a master key for the session.

text: It is made from three keyholders' shares, used for that one session, and always revoked at the end.
prefix: It is made from three keyholders' shares, used for that one session, and always revoked at the end.

text: So no master key sits around, waiting to be stolen.
prefix: So no master key sits around, waiting to be stolen.

text: And backups.

text: Card numbers in the database are sealed by Vault's keys.
prefix: Card numbers in the database are sealed by Vault's keys.

text: A database backup without that Vault is unreadable.

text: So the database and Vault are always backed up together, and restored together.

text: Back in the server room, Timur starts the card zone's installer.

text: It says Vault is new, and that each of the five keyholders copies their own share straight into their own password manager.

text: Three keyholders step up, one at a time, and type their shares unseen: first to unseal Vault, then to make the session's master key.
